thread:
Priya: FYI customer (acct 9987) reporting intermittent 429s across a 30s window — looks like a short spike. They say their app sent a big fan-out and then got a steady stream of 429s. attaching logs they pasted.
Samir: Can you paste the raw headers they got? 429 usually shows Retry-After. if they hit burst credits it might return specific headers.
Priya: Here — customer pasted this snippet:
SupportBot: automated-log: [2026-02-18T15:12:03Z] upstream_status=429 x-retry-after=2 x-burst-remaining=0 x-burst-cap=120
Ava: x-burst-remaining=0 is the key. that means they exhausted short-term burst credits on the hosted tier.
Jordan: Quick question: did they have any client-side retries with exponential backoff? often naive SDK retries amplify fan-outs.
Priya: They said they used the JS SDK with default retry behavior — basically immediate retries up to 3x. their pattern: 1 request triggers 10 parallel requests, then each retries -> amplifies.
Samir: Classic retry storm. two things to consider: 1) server-side burst credits/regeneration properties 2) client-side smoothing/local leaky-bucket or jittered backoff.
Ava: For clarity on server side, our burst credit model is token-bucket-like: each customer has a baseline sustained rate and a burst reservoir. burst_cap is proportional to their plan; it regenerates at a fixed rate per second until full. once burst_remaining hits 0 we return 429s until tokens regen.
Priya: Customer asked: how long will it take to regen to serve their spike? they lost 120 burst tokens.
Jordan: If regen_rate = 2 tokens/sec (hosted standard), then 120 tokens -> ~60s to recover. but exact regen depends on plan and time-weighted window.
Priya: They want to avoid this in future. suggested steps?
Samir: On one-off spikes: implement client-side smoothing. Example leaky bucket algorithm or token-bucket limiter on the client with a small queue and jittered exponential backoff for retries. Also respect Retry-After header.
Ava: Example config we usually suggest to customers (JS pseudocode):

```js
// client-side smoothing pseudo-config
const MAX_CONCURRENCY = 8; // limit parallel calls
const LEAK_RATE = 10; // tokens/sec allowed
const RETRY_OPTIONS = { retries: 4, baseDelayMs: 200, jitter: true };
```

Priya: Also suggested: request upgrade to Dedicated or set a higher burst cap / reserved capacity for predictable high-fanout workloads.
Jordan: For support troubleshooting: repro steps I used locally to simulate their pattern:
1) start 50 concurrent requests at t=0
2) each request retries up to 3 times with no jitter
3) observe x-burst-remaining header drop to 0 and 429 flood

Logs:
```
15:12:02 request id=abc status=200 tokens_left=15
15:12:03 request id=def status=429 x-burst-remaining=0
15:12:03 request id=ghi status=429 retry-after=2
```
Samir: Recommendation email draft to customer:
- add client-side concurrency cap (<=8)
- add jittered backoff and honor Retry-After
- consider reserved capacity if you have predictable spikes
- we can whitelist specific IPs or increase burst cap temporarily for migration tests
Ava: One more thing: if they cannot change clients (third-party SDK) we can enable an ingress-side smoothing proxy on their Dedicated or via a partner edge — essentially queue + rate limiter in front of the API.
Priya: Customer asked for timeline to get temporary bump. OpsEngine, can we do a one-off burst boost for acct 9987 for next 10 mins?
OpsEngine: @Priya I can add a temporary policy that increases burst_cap by 300 for 15 minutes. will log ACL change and notify. doing it now.
SupportBot: policy-change: burst_cap bumped by 300 for account 9987 until 2026-02-18T15:27:00Z by OpsEngine
Priya: sent instructions to customer about client changes and asked if they'd like the temporary bump. they said yes and confirmed reduced retries + concurrency cap applied.
Jordan: Follow-up: add a KB article for "Handling short-term spikes and burst credits" with sample SDK configs and repro patterns. this thread can be source.
Samir: I'll retroactively add monitoring alert that triggers when x-burst-remaining <= 10 for any account for >30s so we proactively reach out.
Priya: Perfect. closing loop with customer in 30m and will paste final notes here.
Ava: :thumbsup:
